initiators: Pro Schweiz, unterstützt u.a. von der SVP
summary: The initiative would enshrine perpetual, armed neutrality in the Constitution. Switzerland would not join or cooperate with military alliances unless attacked or facing imminent attack, take part in military conflicts between other states, or impose sanctions on belligerent states, except UN sanctions and anti-circumvention measures.

initiators: Verein «Sauberes Trinkwasser für alle», unterstützt von Umwelt- und Tierschutzorganisationen
summary: The initiative demands that at least 70 per cent of the food consumed in Switzerland be produced domestically, with agriculture producing more plant-based and fewer animal-based foods and using fewer plant protection products and fertilisers. Targets are to be achieved within ten years of adoption.

title_en: VAT increase in favour of the old-age insurance
summary: The federal decree would raise value-added tax by 0.4 percentage points, except on certain everyday goods such as food and medicines, to finance part of the 13th OASI pension payment. The increase could enter into force at the start of 2028 at the earliest.

initiators: Schweizer Tierschutz STS, Stiftung für das Tier im Recht (TIR), Fondation Franz Weber, Vier Pfoten
summary: The initiative demands a ban on the sale and use of fireworks that produce noise. Cantons could grant exemptions for events of supra-regional significance, such as the National Day on 1 August, but individuals would still not be allowed to set off noisy fireworks.

title_en: Initiative on the taxation of married couples
summary: The initiative demands that married couples' incomes remain combined for direct federal tax and that married couples not be disadvantaged compared with other taxpayers. Without an implementing law in force by 2030, married couples would pay the lower of joint and separate tax calculations.

title_en: Amendment to the War Materiel Act
initiators: SP, Grüne, EVP, PdA, GSoA, verschiedene Hilfswerke u.a.
summary: The amendment would allow war materiel exports to partner states involved in an armed conflict if compatible with neutrality and Swiss foreign and security interests. In exceptional circumstances, the Federal Council could depart from the authorisation criteria; non-re-export assurances would no longer always be required.

title_en: Initiative to ban the import of foie gras
summary: The initiative demands a constitutional ban on importing foie gras and foie gras products. Parliament would have to issue implementing provisions within two years of acceptance; if these are not in force by then, the Federal Council would issue them by ordinance in the interim.

initiators: Aktion Vierviertel, unterstützt u.a. von SP, Grünen und Operation Libero
summary: The initiative demands that the Confederation regulate naturalisation. Foreign applicants would be entitled to citizenship after five years' lawful residence, provided they have not been sentenced to a long-term prison term, do not endanger Switzerland's security and have basic knowledge of a national language.

initiators: Bündnis aus SP, Grünen, Umwelt-, Menschenrechts- und Entwicklungszusammenarbeitsorganisationen
summary: The federal decree approves the economic partnership agreement of 23 June 2025 between the EFTA states and Malaysia. The agreement covers, among other things, tariff relief, trade in services, investment, intellectual property, public procurement, and trade-related environmental issues and labour standards.

title_en: Nuclear Energy Act (lifting of the ban on the construction of new nuclear power plants)
initiators: SP, Grüne, GLP, Mitte-Frauen und Umweltorganisationen
summary: The amendment to the Nuclear Energy Act would lift the ban on building new nuclear power plants by repealing the ban on granting general licences for them. Such a licence would additionally require that financing of construction and operation be secured.

title_en: Priority of collective employment agreements over cantonal minimum wages
summary: Minimum wages in collective employment agreements declared generally binding would take precedence over differing cantonal law. Where cantonal minimum wages prevail when the amendment enters into force, they would remain applicable at that level until the agreement's minimum wages exceed them.
